fields.office: Office of Security Policy and Industry Engagement
fields.subject: Airport Operational Database Integrity
fields.applicability: All airport operators regulated under 49 CFR 1542.103(a)
fields.purpose:
TSA has received information that an unauthorized party gained administrative access to the airport operational database (AODB) at a U.S. commercial airport and altered flight, gate and destination data published to flight information displays, baggage sortation and public address systems. The intrusion originated from a phished workstation on the operator's network.

Inaccurate flight data at screening checkpoints and gates creates crowding, misdirected passengers and boarding-pass validation failures. This Security Directive requires immediate verification of data integrity and of access controls for systems that feed passenger-facing information.
actions: Within 24 hours, verify that all data published to flight information displays, baggage systems and automated public address systems matches carrier source data.
Within 24 hours, reset credentials for all administrative accounts on the AODB and associated database servers, and remove shared or default administrator accounts.
Within 72 hours, restrict administrative access to the AODB to designated workstations on a segregated network segment.
Report any unauthorized access or data manipulation to the TSA Operations Center within 12 hours of discovery.
Maintain a manual passenger information procedure (whiteboards, live announcements) that can be activated within 30 minutes.
fields.contact: Direct questions about this Security Directive to your TSA Federal Security Director.
